_note: Validator partition scenarios derived from postfiatd commit 0085a1ff885d6a446369cf73a4430f75af22be55. All expected_behavior statements are derived from pinned-code rules; every scenario carries a 'source' field citing file:line. Quorum rule throughout (identical UNL): max(ceil(effectiveUNL*0.67), ceil(UNL*0.60)). Modelled close time 4 s/ledger unless stated; close time is emergent in the code, not a constant.

scenarios.expected_behavior: Majority side A (7 validators) collects 7 trusted validations per ledger, reaches quorum 7, and validates every ledger it closes. Minority side B (3 validators) collects 3 validations, never reaches quorum, so its ledgers close by consensus but are never validated: its validated sequence stalls while consensus rounds keep running (stalled/MovedOn/Expired exits, no deadlock). On heal, side B detects preferred-ledger divergence, discards its 40 unvalidated ledgers, and re-acquires side A's chain; final ledger hashes reconcile.
scenarios.name: Minority/majority split 7/3

partition.note: Clean split: no cross-side traffic for 40 ledgers, then full heal.

scenarios.expected_behavior: Side A (6 validators) receives validations from both sides (6 own + 4 from B = 10) and reaches quorum 7, so it validates every ledger. Side B (4 validators) receives only its own 4 validations, never reaches quorum 7, and stalls validation while its consensus rounds keep running. The asymmetry is visible only in validation counts, not in peer counts: B sees A's proposals but A never sees B's acknowledgements of A's ledgers. On heal both sides reconcile to A's chain.

scenarios.expected_behavior: While the link is down (5-ledger windows) the network is a 5/5 split and neither side reaches quorum 7, so no ledger validates on either side; consensus rounds still run and close ledgers. While the link is up (5-ledger windows) the full 10-validator set validates every ledger. No side ever validates alone, so no persistent fork forms: the only validated chain is the one built during up windows. Flapping therefore costs validation liveness (30 of 60 ledgers unvalidated) without creating a dual-validated fork.

scenarios.expected_behavior: The two sides trust divergent UNLs, so BOTH sides validate concurrently and a true dual-validated fork persists for the whole partition. Side A trusts 8 validators (its 7 plus validator 7); its quorum is max(ceil(8*0.67)=6, ceil(8*0.60)=5)=6 and it collects 7 validations. Side B trusts 7 validators (its 5 plus validators 0,1); its quorum is max(ceil(7*0.67)=5, ceil(7*0.60)=5)=5 and it collects 5 validations. Each side's chain is quorum-validated, so neither side's checkAccept stalls and preferred-ledger selection cannot resolve the fork until the UNLs reconverge. On heal the side with larger branch support wins (LedgerTrie getPreferred) and the loser discards its validated ledgers.
scenarios.name: UNL subset isolation (divergent UNLs, dual validation)

scenarios.expected_behavior: A flag ledger (sequence 8283904, seq % 256 == 0) falls inside the partition. Voting happens on the pre-flag ledger: side A counts 7 trusted validations, all voting yes, which exceeds the post-fix threshold (7 > 7*67/100 = 4.69), so side A records tfGotMajority in its next ledger. Side B counts 3 trusted validations with 1 yes vote; 1 > 3*67/100 = 2.01 is false, so side B records no majority and its amendment clock freezes (no voting at all would occur if it were below quorum: onClose requires >= quorum() trusted validations). Neither side enables the amendment inside the scenario: the 2-week hold (1,209,600 s) needs 302,400 ledgers at the modelled 4 s/ledger close, far beyond the 60-ledger window. On heal, the surviving majority timestamps are side A's, because only its chain is validated.
scenarios.name: Amendment-vote split across a flag ledger

scenarios.expected_behavior: The minority side (3 validators) keeps running consensus rounds but never validates: every round ends via the stalled-dispute shortcut, MovedOn, or Expired/bow-out exits, never via quorum. Close-time consensus (75%) is never reached inside the minority side, whose three validators' close-time votes disagree with each other (modelled clock drift under partition), so its close-time resolution coarsens one bin per ledger (30 -> 60 -> 90 -> 120 s) and its ledgers carry the sLCF_NoConsensusTime flag (closeFlags 0x01). The majority side (7 validators) validates normally with resolution refining toward 10-20 s bins. The minority's close-time drift is an observable partition signal, not a halt.
scenarios.name: Ledger-close stall with close-time drift

scenarios.expected_behavior: The isolated validator (9) has 0 peers, below minPeerCount, so its operating mode is DISCONNECTED and consensus is not ticked at all (NetworkOPs heartbeat gate). It closes no ledgers and validates nothing while isolated. The remaining 9 validators collect 9 trusted validations, reach quorum 7, and validate every ledger. On heal, the isolated node re-enters CONNECTED, its preferred ledger differs from its local LCL, handleWrongLedger fires, and it acquires the majority chain ledger by ledger (each missing ledger costs at most ~21 s of InboundLedger attempts: initial + 6 retries at 3 s). No fork is created: a single validator cannot validate alone.
scenarios.name: Single-validator isolation

scenarios.expected_behavior: No partition exists, but 2 of 3 list publishers are unavailable while listThreshold_ is 2 (majority of 3 publishers). The unavailable-publisher count (2) reaches min(listThreshold_, N - listThreshold_ + 1) = min(2, 2) = 2, so calculateQuorum returns SIZE_MAX: quorum is disabled and NOTHING validates on any node, even though all 10 validators are connected and agree. Consensus rounds still close ledgers. When the publishers return, updateTrusted recomputes quorum 7 and validation resumes from the next close. Publisher outage is a whole-network validation freeze, not a partition.
scenarios.name: Publisher outage disables quorum

scenarios.expected_behavior: The 7/3 split lasts 200 ledgers at a modelled 4 s/ledger = 800 s of simulated time. Pre-partition validations go stale: WALL 5 min (300 s, 75 ledgers) and LOCAL 3 min (180 s, 45 ledgers) pass first, then the validation SET expires at 10 min (600 s, 150 ledgers) and Validations::expire sweeps the minority side's pre-partition sets. After ledger 150 the minority side holds no usable pre-partition validation for any ledger; on heal it cannot shortcut rejoin from stale sets and must re-acquire the majority chain fresh (40+ ledgers of its own chain are unvalidated and discarded). The majority side is unaffected: it keeps receiving fresh validations inside every window. The cascade is time-driven, not count-driven: a shorter partition would not trigger it.
scenarios.name: Validation-expiry cascade (long partition)

scenarios.expected_behavior: After a 7/3 split of 40 ledgers, the heal is a race between the minority side's unvalidated chain and the majority's validated chain. Preferred-ledger selection (branch support) picks the majority chain: its branch support is 7 trusted validations per ledger against the minority's 3. The minority side's handleWrongLedger fires, it stops proposing, replays stored proposals, and acquires the majority chain via InboundLedger: 40 ledgers re-fetched, each on the first 3 s attempt (peers hold them), 0 timeouts, worst-case bound 40 x ~21 s if peers lacked them. Every minority ledger whose parent hash mismatches the adopted chain is invalidated by setFullLedger (hash-chained reconciliation, not transaction replay). Final ledger hashes match across all 10 validators; 0 minority ledgers survive as canonical.
scenarios.name: Rejoin hash-reconciliation race
